subject: Dedicated capacity recommendation & ops playbook for Sparkle Inc: H100/A100/L4 mix
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@sparkle.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity recommendation & ops playbook for Sparkle Inc: H100/A100/L4 mix

Hi Emma — great call this morning. As promised, I put together a recommendation and an ops playbook for Sparkle's Dedicated deployment that balances cost, latency SLOs, and reliability for the three primary workloads you called out: user-facing chat (short contexts, strict P95 latency), large-document summarization (long context, throughput-sensitive), and embeddings/batching (high throughput, lower latency requirements).

High-level recommendation (summary):
- Primary fleet: mix of L4 + H100 with a small A100 reserve.
  - L4 pool (40%): handle chat and embeddings at low cost and excellent token/sec for short contexts and embeddings throughput.
  - H100 pool (50%): serve long-context summarization and retrieval-augmented generation where memory and FP16 perf matter.
  - A100 reserve (10%): compatibility tier for heavy KV-cache / legacy quantized models and as an overflow for bursty long sequences.

Why this mix?
- Memory vs perf: H100 gives higher HBM capacity and matrix perf for long sequences and large batch KV cache. L4 is extremely cost-efficient for <8k contexts and embeddings. A100 sits in the middle and provides predictable FP16 throughput for some quantized variants you may want to pin.
- Ops & reliability: we recommend pinning your mission-critical model to H100 with a fallback policy that routes to A100 or a smaller L4 ensemble when H100 capacity is saturated (graceful degradation on quality).

Attached: a capacity model (sparkle_capacity_model_v2.xlsx) with projection by concurrency and expected qps, and a latency/throughput chart (sku_latency_tradeoffs.png). See the Drive link in-line if you want the live workbook.

Next steps I suggest:
1) We spin up a small canary for your chat product on L4 (2 instances) and the summarization pipeline on H100 (1 instance) for 2 weeks.
2) Run the workload profiler (we'll share the script) across the canary to capture real seq-length distribution and prefix cache hit rates.
3) After profiling, we finalize exact node counts and reservation tiers (monthly commit) + define a burst pool for the A100 reserve.

Operational notes:
- Autoscaling: use CPU-meta autoscaling for the L4 pool to preserve latency; use queue-depth based scaling for H100 to maximize throughput.
- KV cache: for long-context jobs pin to H100 to avoid cross-node KV cache thrash.
- Cost control: set a per-route token cap and rate limits; Redwood Optimize can propose quantization for summarization that cuts cost up to ~30% with minimal quality drop (we can run evals).

Emma — can you confirm the SLOs we should target (P95 latency in ms) for chat vs summarization and whether you'd like the A100 reserve to be billed as burst or reserved capacity? Once you confirm, we'll lock the canary start date.

Thanks,

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Emma Li <emma@sparkle.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity recommendation & ops playbook for Sparkle Inc: H100/A100/L4 mix

Thanks Ava — added a few technical clarifications after reviewing the profiler expectations and the projected concurrency in the spreadsheet. Quick notes for the team and for Emma: 

- Sequence-length distribution: your canary should emit traces with a realistic mix. If you see >5% of requests >32k tokens, shift the long-context pool to H100-heavy and consider model-splitting (chunk+stitch) to avoid extreme HBM usage.
- Batch sizing: L4 supports larger micro-batches for embeddings; target 128 items/batch for embeddings and 1-8 for chat depending on latency. For summarization on H100, we recommend dynamic batching with a max batch window of 50ms to preserve P95 under load.
- KV cache memory: H100 (80GB HBM) comfortably holds larger KV caches per-shard; A100 (40GB/80GB depending on SKU) can be used for smaller shards but will increase inter-shard traffic if you split sequences. 
- Quantization: if Sparkle wants aggressive cost cuts for summarization, we can test 4-bit quantization on H100-compatible kernels — this preserves quality in most cases but needs evals. L4 has strong int8 pathways for embeddings and small-chat models.
- Fallback routing: implement a priority routing table: H100 primary -> A100 fallback -> L4 degraded-response mode (lower max tokens / summarization chunking). This preserves service availability.

Operational checklist for canary startup (I attached the updated capacity sheet):
- Canary metrics dashboard: P50/P95/P99 latency, tokens/sec, cache hit rate, GPU utilization per-pool.
- Alerting: GPU OOMs, queue growth > threshold, and sustained >85% GPU utilization for 5 min trigger auto-scale or operator paging.
- Runbook snippets: how to cordon a node, redeploy a quantized model, and flip routing during a region outage.

I also added an appendix with expected cost per-token numbers across pools under typical chat vs summarization loads.

-Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

Thanks Ava and Dev — this is really helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we greenlight the canary: 

1) SLOs: For chat we want P95 < 220ms (mobile clients). For summarization batch jobs we target average latency < 1.2s but can accept higher P99 during heavy archival processing.
2) Burst billing: procurement prefers burst pool billed as pay-as-you-go rather than a committed A100 reserve to start — can we size an A100 burst pool that will be available within 5 minutes of triggering?
3) Data controls: we need to ensure KV cache entries for user uploads are not persisted beyond 30 days and are rotatable via our KMS key. Can you add a short note on compliance settings for the canary?

If those look feasible, procurement is ready to sign the gate contract for a 3-month trial with the option to convert to reserved capacity.

Best,
Emma
Head of Product, Sparkle Inc
emma@sparkle.ai

Emma — all feasible. Quick responses inline: 

1) SLOs: P95 < 220ms for chat — we'll build the canary dashboards to measure P50/P95/P99 and will set an initial autoscale policy that keeps P95 under 200ms in test. Summarization avg <1.2s is reasonable; we'll accept higher tail during batch windows.

2) Burst billing: we can provision an on-demand A100 burst pool (pay-as-you-go) with warm standby nodes in the same region; typical spin-up time with warm-standby is <3 minutes. We'll size it to handle up to 30% additional summarization concurrency in first pass. If you prefer instant cold-starts without warm standby, latency to availability will be longer and we recommend a small reserved buffer.

3) Data controls/KMS: for the canary we'll enable 30-day TTL on KV cache entries and enforce KMS rotation on the key every 90 days (configurable). We'll also enable audit logging for all cache fetches and model access. I'll ask Security to include the compliance snippet in the trial contract.

Next steps:
- Procurement: sign the 3-month gate contract.
- Ops: we schedule canary start Monday 12/07 at 09:00 PT. Dev will run the profiler script in the first 48 hours.
- AE: I'll prepare the canary runbook and a short handoff to Sparkle's infra team.

Attaching the capacity sheet and the latency tradeoff PNG again. Let me know if procurement needs alternate billing terms; we can map them in the HubSpot deal.

Thanks — excited to get this running.
